segments.text: Logging in as bandit thirty-two drops us into a strange restricted shell: it uppercases every command before running it.
I log in as bandit32 with ssh bandit32@bandit.labs.overthewire.org -p 2220.
The note states the trap: the login shell uppercases every command before running it, so ordinary commands become garbage.
The trick is to use something uppercasing cannot change: dollar zero has no letters, so it survives, and in a shell it expands to the shell itself.
Running it starts a fresh normal shell.
From there I run id, which reports uid eleven thousand and thirty-three, bandit thirty-three.
Then I cat bandit thirty-three's password file.
It prints the password for bandit thirty-three, and the level is solved.
